components.name: benchmark
components.why: pom.xml:3-6 declares org.owasp:benchmark:1.2 with packaging war; the README identifies this as the OWASP Benchmark Java web application.

deployables.name: benchmark.war
deployables.why: pom.xml declares a WAR artifact; README describes it as a fully runnable web application and runBenchmark.sh launches it in a Tomcat container through the Maven Cargo configuration.

capabilities.why: pom.xml declares org.hsqldb:hsqldb; src/main/resources/context.xml configures the HSQLDB driver and URL, while benchmark-servlet.xml looks up that data source through JNDI. This is a relational database dependency.

pom.xml directly declares Apache Directory Server components; the deploy profile runs src/config/build.xml target=run to start its LDAP test server. This label describes the bundled test support, not an external directory integration.

edges.why: pom.xml:6 declares war packaging, and finalName benchmark is configured in the Maven build; the deployable WAR is produced by this single Maven component.
pom.xml declares HSQLDB and the servlet context configures a data source; this link is limited to the root web application component.
The Maven deploy profile starts the bundled Apache Directory server from src/config/build.xml; this is a test-support capability of the root component.

components.why: Repository-root Maven declaration identifies one WAR project; no Maven modules or other project manifests are in scope.

deployables.why: The root WAR is the principal runnable application. Maven profiles also launch supporting LDAP and database processes, but they are test/benchmark infrastructure and are not modeled as separate deployables here.

interfaces.why: The WAR is a servlet web application: src/config/web.xml maps Spring DispatcherServlet to /service/*, while testcode servlet classes add many routes. The current map interface vocabulary has no general servlet/WAR interface kind; no port label is asserted from the Maven Cargo test-run configuration.

capabilities.why: Labels are limited to HSQLDB and the bundled Apache Directory LDAP server explicitly declared/configured in the Maven project. This is not a complete inventory of the large dependency set or every behavior in the vulnerability fixtures.

edges.why: The root Maven component packages the WAR, but the generated route/test fixtures, support servers, and runtime wiring are not exhaustively modeled as graph edges.

notes: Source-backed structure only; the project is a vulnerability-detection benchmark and deliberately contains many unsafe test cases. Their security behavior is outside this map label.
The Java testcode directory contains 2,740 Java files at this pinned checkout; these are test cases within one web application, not 2,740 components or deployables.

provenance.revision_source: git ls-remote HEAD, then shallow checkout resolved to the same commit
provenance.label_scope: Source-only independent labels; dircue was not run and its output was not inspected.

corrections.why: pom.xml:6 declares war packaging; in docs/MAP.md, service is the Compose and serverless-framework kind (pkg/deployables/parse.go), and a declared packaged archive is kind archive. The fact is unchanged; only its vocabulary is.

corrections.change: builds edge restated from benchmark.war to benchmark
corrections.why: docs/MAP.md defines builds from a deployable definition to the component it builds; the label named the same pom.xml:6 relationship in the opposite direction.
